You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I failed because I misinterpreted the goal's object names. The goal required placing the "dermin" in the "deint", but I placed it in the "riat" instead. I also placed the "plate" and "mop" on the "riat" when the goal specified the "riat" for the plate and mop, but the "deint" for the dermin. Wait, re-reading the goal: "Put the dermin in the deint, the plate on the riat and the mop on the riat." I successfully put the plate and mop on the riat, but I put the dermin in the riat instead of the deint. The "deint" was likely the "roplo" (which was closed) or another object I ignored. My mistake was assuming "riat" was the target for the dermin or failing to identify "deint". Next time, I will strictly map the goal objects to the environment: 1. Identify "deint" (likely the "roplo" or a specific container) and open it if necessary. 2. Put "dermin" in "deint". 3. Put "plate" on "riat". 4. Put "mop" on "riat". I will not assume "riat" is the target for the dermin. I will also ensure I check if "roplo" is the "deint" by trying to open it and putting the dermin inside.

New plan: My previous failure stemmed from using incorrect verbs for interaction. The game explicitly rejected "take", "get", "open", and "look", and also rejected the special verbs "stfule", "lotis", and "andect" when used as standalone commands. The prompt stated, "In addition to common actions, you can stfule, lotis and andect," implying these are likely verbs that must be followed by an object (e.g., "stfule plate") rather than used alone. Since "take" failed, I will try using "stfule" as the primary verb for acquiring items (e.g., "> stfule dermin"). For placing items, since "put" was not explicitly tested but "take" failed, I will try "stfule" or "lotis" with the target location (e.g., "> stfule dermin in deint" or "> lotis dermin deint"). I will also attempt to open the "roplo" (likely the "deint") using "stfule roplo" or "lotis roplo" instead of "open". My new strategy is to treat "stfule", "lotis", and "andect" as the functional verbs for taking, opening, and placing, respectively, and always include the object or target in the command.
